contexts.text: Under Beast, see these references. AC 1361:2. AC 2781.
When oxen and bullocks appear in the World of Spirits, they know that the Angels are talking about natural goods.
A bullock, or son of an ox = what is celestial natural; or what is the same, natural good.
A bullock for sin = the Lord's Divine Natural.
Bullocks and rams = spiritual things.
Heifers and bullocks () = what is of the natural man.
Bullocks () = the good of innocence or of charity in the external or natural man... because calves and bullocks are of a more tender age than oxen. Illustrated.
A bullock of an ox, in the sacrifice of sin, and a ram for a burnt-offering = the purification of good from evils in the external and in the internal man.

Take one bullock a son of the herd () = the purification of the natural or external man. A bullock = the good of innocence and of charity in the natural or external man; and as it is called a son of the herd, the truth of that good is also signified. AC 9990:2.

Thou shalt cause a bullock to approach () = the state of the application of the natural or external man such as he is in his infancy. A bullock = the good of charity and of innocence in the natural or external man.

Thou shalt kill the bullock before Jehovah () = the preparation for the purification of good and truth from the Lord in the external or natural man... The bullock = the purification of the external or natural man.

Thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock () = Divine truth accommodated to the natural or external man... The bullock = the natural man which is to be purified, and in which truth and good are to be implanted.

The flesh of the bullock () = the evil of the former loves there... The bullock = the external or Natural; for in a good sense, a bullock, and a calf = the external or Natural of man as to the good of innocence and of charity; but in the opposite sense, the external or Natural of man as to the evil which is contrary to the good of innocence and of charity.
A bullock () = the good of innocence in the external man.

A bullock of sin thou shalt offer every day on the propitiations () = the continual removal of evils and thence of falsities in the natural man through the good of innocence from the Lord. A bullock = the good of innocence in the natural man.
A bullock = the external good of innocence. AC 10137:10.
Oxen and bullocks correspond to the affections of the natural mind.
That bullocks, and calves = the good of the natural man, Illustrated.
To render the bullocks of the lips () = to confess and give thanks from the goods of doctrine.
Bullocks () = spiritual natural good, which is the good of charity.
